findings_and_questions.first_contract: compile_window_leaf derives board/came counts from each admitted width or height divided by 0.19, casts to usize and iterates without a work budget. CuboidDimensions and LeafDimensions permit arbitrarily large finite positive values; float division can overflow to infinity and Rust float-to-integer cast saturates to usize::MAX. The loop does not stop on the Builder’s latched first error. Both the operable cache and fixed-detail source call this function, but ordinary producer bounds were not assessed. Memory exhaustion or other limits can terminate first; no runtime occurrence or exact duration is claimed.
findings_and_questions.condition: An oversized accepted extent reaches either consumer or the public function. The target usize width affects count. No claim that ordinary generated buildings reach the extreme or that every input is problematic.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Determine caller/author admission and an explicit per-leaf work budget, then preserve fixed zero-valid cuboids, positive operable leaves, first-error semantics and deterministic geometry behavior.

findings_and_questions.kind: bounded historical question refined, no new unique count
findings_and_questions.first_contract: A positive, finite width below 0.002 m is admissible for LeafDimensions. For a timber shutter it gives one board, whose computed width subtracts 0.002 m; CuboidDimensions rejects that negative extent, Builder retains the first error, and compile_window_leaf returns it. The operable ClosureMeshes cache propagates that error, and the SceneWindow Add observer returns before inserting presentation components. This is a mathematical source inference, not a runtime observation.
findings_and_questions.condition: A TimberShutter of such a width must reach this path; normal authored/generated bounds and whether this fallible API should accept or reject every positive extent have not been established. Callback error handling, retry and terminal visibility have not been traced.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Determine supported minimum shutter geometry and its owner; either admit that constraint at the correct boundary or define fallible presentation semantics without weakening geometry roles for fixed/degenerate glazing.
historical_relations: 059 Q-L12-03a885cbf03ba414fc2c expressly held tiny shutter width, producer and native error policy open. /root/lens12_frontier recorded the same negative derived board condition in READ-L12-852; this current source trace refines that existing question, not a newly accepted finding.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: compile_operable_windows indexes public resolved solids in a BTreeMap keyed by ID, selecting the first referenced existing solid with LeadedGlazing or OpeningClosure role. Duplicate IDs are last-wins; missing or wrong-role references are skipped, while owner equality is not checked. If a bad reference or duplicate resolves to an unrelated same-role solid, the compiled window takes its leaf type, source and geometry. The sibling door compiler has a different predicate and source result.
findings_and_questions.condition: This requires a malformed or independently modified plan reaching the compiler, or an allowed producer relation selecting an unrelated same-role solid. The expected meaning and ordering of multiple closure layers and whole-graph validity remain open.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Establish reference uniqueness, owner, role, layer ordering and error semantics at the plan owner and exact consumer before deciding common repair boundaries. Preserve the intended selectable roles and optional layers.
historical_relations: Related to prior packet P16-DOOR-CLOSURE-SELECTION-CONTRACT and prior P16-COLLISION-SELECTED-IDENTITY-LOSS, not an automatic alias or new unique count. The window-specific role filter makes its join contract different.
059 Q-L11-bd78dd3a8b1d3d580761 and Q-L12-5cc02ecd5125d414e1f4 leave whole-plan acceptance and connected collision relationships open.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: WindowSpec has independently checked public positions, positive leaf dimensions, normalized tangent/outward, angles and bar-presence. Deserialize reconstructs each leaf and maps a geometry cause to an opening/source-associated serde diagnostic, but does not check their aggregate pose, hinge, swing or source relationship. Its source producer derives inward swing using tangent/outward and its server consumer retains and uses those fields.
findings_and_questions.condition: A separately constructed or decoded incoherent WindowSpec must reach a consumer that assumes these relations; not all constructors, trust boundaries, physical frames or consumer policy are covered. Intentional independent bar presence and frame differences cannot be declared invalid by shape alone.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Identify the correct owner for any cross-field/frame relationship and validate only its intended domain; retain the distinct checked leaf and diagnostic boundaries.
historical_relations: 059 successor-103 and READ-L12-852 explicitly retained aggregate pose questions; this current consumer source adds bounded evidence without historical credit transfer.
